name: Ca-alginate sacrificial network + cellulose/CNF scaffold
primary_failure_mechanism: water ingress plus Ca2+ loss/monovalent-ion exchange leading to gel-sol transition
reason_to_keep: Strongest current passive mechanism evidence: calcium alginate can exhibit swelling followed by dissolution after ion exchange; cellulose/CNF can reinforce alginate hydrogels

name: Delayed citrate-triggered Ca-alginate network + cellulose/CNF scaffold
sacrificial_or_failure_phase: Ca2+-crosslinked alginate plus delayed/compartmentalized citrate source
primary_failure_mechanism: after an induction period citrate transport/availability accelerates Ca2+ sequestration and loss of alginate network stiffness
reason_to_keep: 4% alginate in-situ rheology shows external sodium citrate can reduce G-prime by about one order of magnitude after Ca crosslinking; a delayed internal citrate front could make lifetime more programmable than passive ion loss, but delayed-release chemistry and safe concentration are unproven

name: Pullulan sacrificial binder + cellulose fibre scaffold
primary_failure_mechanism: hydration/plasticization followed by binder solubilization and fibre-network loss of cohesion
reason_to_keep: Mechanistically distinct from ionic gel failure; pullulan is water-soluble and its blends have tunable mechanical/solubilization behaviour

name: Ca-pectin sacrificial network + cellulose scaffold
primary_failure_mechanism: Ca-crosslink dissociation plus swelling and mechanical fatigue
reason_to_keep: Plant-derived alternative ionotropic polysaccharide; calcium pectin gels show swelling and eventual dissolution as free calcium falls, but mechanism overlaps A01
